I’m more concerned with whether the next step can be delivered than with the upgrade narrative of ETH.

An announcement released by the Ethereum Foundation on September 28 shows that the Glamssterdam plan is scheduled to be activated on the Sepolia testnet at 21:53:36 Beijing time on October 6; as of this verification, the activation time for Hoodi on the mainnet has not yet been determined.

This means a visible technical milestone has been lined up, but there’s still a validation process before the mainnet can go live. Calling the testnet plan directly a “mainnet bullish signal already realized” would skip the most critical part.

The key points in the announcement include incorporating the separation of block proposers and builders into the protocol, as well as a block-level access list—aimed at laying the groundwork for higher execution throughput. At the same time, gas fee rules have been adjusted, and applications need to verify compatibility; this does not automatically mean that all users’ fees will drop immediately.

My priority order is: whether the testnet activation proceeds as scheduled, whether clients and applications adapt smoothly, and then whether there’s a clear mainnet timeline afterward. These developments help judge whether the narrative continues moving forward more than a simple “the upgrade will make prices rise.”

For $ETH , technical progress and market pricing are two lines that need to be observed simultaneously. Successful test execution can increase confidence in implementation, but it cannot directly prove that prices will rise; if key arrangements are adjusted, time expectations should be reassessed as well.

I’m optimistic about using real progress to test the upgrade narrative, rather than pricing all expectations in as already-granted positives ahead of time.

ETH的升级叙事，我更在意下一步能不能兑现。

以太坊基金会9月28日发布的公告显示，Glamsterdam计划于北京时间10月6日21:53:36在Sepolia测试网激活；截至本次核查，Hoodi与主网激活时间仍未确定。

这意味着，一个可观察的技术节点已经排上日程，但距离主网落地还有验证过程。把测试网计划直接说成“主网利好已经兑现”，会跳过最关键的一段。

公告中的重点包括把区块提议者与构建者的分离纳入协议，以及区块级访问列表，目标是为更高的执行吞吐量提供基础。同时，Gas计费规则也有调整，应用需要验证兼容性；这并不等于所有用户的手续费都会立刻下降。

我的关注顺序是：测试网激活是否按计划进行，客户端和应用是否平稳适配，随后是否出现明确的主网安排。这些进展比一句“升级就会涨”更能帮助判断叙事有没有继续向前走。

对$ETH 而言，技术进度与市场定价是两条需要同时观察的线。测试顺利可以增加对实施的信心，却不能直接证明价格将上涨；若关键安排调整，也应重新评估时间预期。

我看好用真实进度检验升级叙事，而不是提前把所有预期算成已经到手的利好。

SEC is considering easing crypto custody rules! Institutional entry threshold may be lowered

The U.S. SEC is advancing new rules for the custody of crypto assets.
The latest proposal plans to adjust how investment advisers and regulated funds hold Crypto assets, providing a clearer compliance path for institutions to manage digital assets.

Key changes include:
① Allow self-custody of Crypto assets in some cases
If there is no suitable qualified custodian, after meeting safety, recordkeeping, and risk-control requirements, an investment adviser may custody clients’ crypto assets itself.

② Expand compliant custody options
The SEC proposes to allow qualifying state-chartered trust companies to act as crypto asset custodians, giving institutions more choices.

Why does it matter?

In the past, many traditional institutions wanted exposure to digital assets such as BTC and ETH, but faced a recurring problem:
Assets can be bought—but who will keep them safely and compliantly?
Custody has long been a major obstacle for Wall Street’s entry into Crypto.

If the new rules are ultimately implemented, they could help drive:
👉 More investment advisers offering crypto asset allocation services
👉 Funds and institutions finding it easier to hold assets such as BTC and ETH
👉 Deeper connections between traditional finance and Crypto

That said, it’s important to note:
This is still only an SEC proposal, not the final rules. It will still need to go through public comments and the regulatory process.

In recent years, the focus of Crypto regulation has been more on:
Issuance
Trading
Securities-like attributes

Now it is gradually shifting toward:
How to help institutions hold digital assets safely and compliantly.

In one sentence:
ETFs open the capital gateway, and custody rules may be addressing the final hurdle for institutions to hold Crypto.

At the same time, centralized exchanges such as Binance also recorded multiple million-dollar liquidations of $BTC and $ETH  short orders. One Ethereum short liquidation, at around 2.1 million USD, was particularly notable. Total liquidation volume was primarily driven by BTC- and ETH-related positions.

By asset, the figures were about $BTC 8833 (units), $ETH 1827 (units), and SOL at 5.15 million. Shorts accounted for nearly more than 90%, indicating that leveraged short exposure was concentratedly liquidated in a short period of time rather than a balanced long/short retracement. Market risk appetite had been recovering beforehand, but the core driver of this pulse was the position structure—not a single policy-driven catalyst.

Such pulses more often reflect position structure and leverage crowding, and should not be interpreted alone as a trend inflection point. Going forward, attention should be paid to how open contracts are reset, whether new short positions are covered at higher price levels, and whether volatility continues to transmit to spot markets and related liquidity conditions.

The Ethereum Foundation launches zkAPI! AI payments enter the privacy era 🔥

Ethereum is seeing another new infrastructure breakthrough.
The Ethereum Foundation, in collaboration with the Open Anonymity Project, has launched zkAPI—which is already live on the Ethereum mainnet.

Its goal is simple:
When users use AI and other API services, they don’t have to reveal their payment identity.

Traditional AI service model:
API Key
↓
Account binding
↓
Payment records
↓
All usage is linked

But zkAPI wants to change that.
It achieves this through **zero-knowledge proofs (ZK Proofs)**:
Users first deposit assets such as ETH and USDC into an Ethereum Vault contract, and then—via a zero-knowledge proof—prove that they have sufficient balance to make payments, without revealing:
❌ Which wallet pays
❌ Which funds were the source
❌ The user’s real identity
AI service providers can receive the request, but they can’t link the request to the payment identity.

Why does this matter?
① In the AI era, privacy becomes a new requirement

In the future, AI Agents may make massive calls to:
AI models
API endpoints
data services
computing resources
If every call is tied to an identity, users’ behaviors could form a complete profile.

zkAPI offers a new way of thinking:
Payment can be verified, but identity can’t be tracked.

② ETH is exploring a role as AI infrastructure
In the past, ETH’s main narratives were:
DeFi
NFT
RWA
Now, it adds:
AI payments
AI agent settlement
economic interactions between machines
If in the future AIs need to autonomously call services, they’ll also require a low-friction payment method.

③ Zero-knowledge proof applications keep expanding
ZK technology is moving from:
private transactions
to:
identity protection
data validation
AI payments
That said, it’s important to note that zkAPI is still an early experimental project and can’t hide everything—for example, network data and the request content itself may still reveal partial clues.

So what’s truly worth关注 this launch isn’t just a tool.

It’s a direction:
When AI starts operating at scale, who will solve machine payments, privacy, and trust issues?
Ethereum is trying to become one of the infrastructures for that.

content:
以太坊基金会推出zkAPI！AI支付进入隐私时代🔥

以太坊又迎来一个新的基础设施进展。
以太坊基金会联合 Open Anonymity Project 推出 zkAPI，目前已经上线 Ethereum 主网。

它的目标很简单：
让用户使用AI等API服务时，不暴露自己的支付身份。

传统AI服务模式：
API Key
↓
账号绑定
↓
支付记录
↓
使用行为全部关联

而zkAPI想改变这一点。
它通过**零知识证明（ZK Proof）**实现：
用户先将ETH、USDC等资产存入以太坊Vault合约，然后通过零知识
证明，证明“自己有足够额度支付”，但不会暴露：
❌ 哪个钱包支付
❌ 哪笔资金来源
❌ 用户真实身份
AI服务商可以收到请求，但无法把请求和付款身份绑定。

为什么这件事重要？
① AI时代，隐私成为新需求

未来AI Agent可能大量调用：
AI模型
API接口
数据服务
计算资源
如果每一次调用都绑定身份，用户行为可能形成完整画像。

zkAPI提供了一种新的思路：
支付可验证，但身份不可追踪。

② ETH正在探索AI基础设施角色
过去ETH主要叙事：
DeFi
NFT
RWA
现在又增加：
AI支付
AI Agent结算
机器之间的经济交互
未来AI之间如果需要自主调用服务，也需要一种低摩擦支付方式。

③ 零知识证明应用继续扩大
ZK技术正在从：
隐私交易
扩展到：
身份保护
数据验证
AI支付
不过需要注意：
zkAPI目前仍属于早期实验性项目，并不能隐藏所有信息，例如网络数据和请求内容本身仍可能暴露部分线索。

所以这次上线真正值得关注的，不只是一个工具。

而是一个方向：
当AI开始大规模运行，谁来解决机器支付、隐私和信任问题？
以太坊正在尝试成为这个基础设施之一。

The SEC plans to establish a custody framework for crypto assets.

The SEC has proposed new rules to set up a dedicated framework for registered investment advisers and regulated fund custodians to custody crypto assets, and to allow, under certain conditions, self-custody and custodial arrangements such as using state trust companies. Market interpretation is more bullish: it directly benefits mainstream assets like BTC and ETH by providing a compliant allocation pathway. This signal is friendlier to institutional allocation routes, but the key is not an immediate price rally. Instead, it further removes custody barriers for institutional advisers and funds to enter crypto investments. If the rules are implemented later, designing crypto strategies with traditional funds should become smoother. In the short term, the focus is on feedback from major asset managers, custodians, and trading platforms during the 60-day comment period. When policy expectations heat up, narratives around compliant exchanges, custody, and ETFs are more likely to attract capital attention.

If feedback during the 60-day comment period from major asset managers, custodians, and trading platforms is positive, then rule advancement is likely to go smoothly. If the controversy is concentrated on self-custody and state trust company arrangements, the market will pay more attention to the implementation timeline. Which do you care more about: “institutional funds entering more smoothly,” or “the timetable for the rules to truly take effect”?

Source: SEC
